verdict.summary: Registering an OAuth integration is self-serve with no review, but other users can't authorize it until you add a privacy policy URL and a terms of service URL. In production the real limits are the customer's plan, not Airtable approval: Free workspaces get 1,000 API calls a month shared across all integrations, and every base allows only 5 requests per second.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Register at airtable.com/create/oauth, use an http://localhost redirect, run the PKCE code flow, then grant your own bases.

timeToProd.assumes: A public integration that reads and writes records with data.records:* and schema.bases:read, once privacy policy and terms URLs are on the integration.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Airtable's docs describe no review step. The only stated gate for sharing is the privacy policy and terms URLs.

prerequisites.why: Integrations are registered at airtable.com/create/oauth, and third-party OAuth is available on all plan types.

prerequisites.item: Public privacy policy and terms of service URLs
prerequisites.why: Without them 'other users will not be able to authorize your integration.'

prerequisites.item: An HTTPS redirect URI (http://localhost is fine for development)
prerequisites.why: HTTPS is required except for localhost. Raw IPs other than localhost, fragments, wildcards and open redirects aren't allowed.

prerequisites.item: PKCE (S256) support in your OAuth client
prerequisites.why: The authorize request carries code_challenge with code_challenge_method=S256, and the verifier is 43–128 characters.

scopeTiers.impact: Covers reading and writing records, reading schema, comments and webhooks: everything a typical agent needs. Access is limited to the bases the user picks during consent.
Lets the agent create tables and fields and list the workspaces and bases it can reach. Still self-serve.
These only work for users on enterprise accounts.
These only work when an enterprise admin authorizes. Useful for governance or admin agents, not general data access.

steps.title: Sign in to Airtable
steps.detail: Use any Airtable account. A Free account is fine for development.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: https://airtable.com/create/oauth redirected to the login page (HTTP 302) on 2026-10-20.

steps.title: Register the OAuth integration
steps.detail: Click Register new OAuth integration, give it a unique name, and add the redirect URL.

steps.title: Choose scopes
steps.detail: Pick least-privilege scopes, for example data.records:read, data.records:write and schema.bases:read, and tick them on the integration.

steps.title: Generate a client secret
steps.detail: Generate one if token requests run on a server. Copy it right away: it can't be recovered, only regenerated, and adding one breaks in-flight requests that don't send it.

steps.title: Implement the PKCE code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://airtable.com/oauth2/v1/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope, state and an S256 code_challenge. Within 10 minutes POST to https://airtable.com/oauth2/v1/token with the code_verifier, using Basic auth if you have a secret.

steps.title: Handle refresh and base discovery
steps.detail: Refresh within 60 minutes, store both rotated tokens, and treat 409 as a recent duplicate refresh. Call the list-bases endpoint on each run, since users can change which bases are granted.

steps.title: Write privacy policy and terms
steps.detail: Draft and publish both pages, including how the agent uses Airtable data and any AI model processing.

steps.title: Add the URLs to the integration
steps.detail: Enter the privacy policy and terms URLs on the integration so other users can authorize it.

steps.title: Test with another account
steps.detail: Authorize from a second Airtable account, pick a base with Add a base, and confirm reads and writes work.

agentCanDo: Choose minimal scopes for the agent's features
Implement PKCE, token exchange and rotating refresh
Throttle to 5 requests/sec per base and back off 30 seconds on 429
Draft the privacy policy and terms pages
Check the OAuth metadata endpoint for scope changes
humanMustDo: Sign in and register the integration
Generate and store the client secret
Publish and enter the privacy policy and terms URLs
Test authorization from a second account

blockers.symptom: Other users can't authorize the integration
blockers.cause: The integration has no privacy policy URL or terms of service URL.
blockers.fix: Add both URLs to the integration.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error screen wasn't described.

blockers.cause: Wrong client_id, or a secret exists but no Basic auth header was sent (or one was sent without a secret).
blockers.fix: Send Authorization: Basic only when the integration has a secret; otherwise put client_id in the body.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed by POSTing a dummy client_id to https://airtable.com/oauth2/v1/token on 2026-10-20.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429, and later requests also fail for about 30 seconds
blockers.cause: More than 5 requests per second to one base, or 50 per second per user.
blockers.fix: Queue requests per base and wait 30 seconds after a 429.

blockers.symptom: API calls blocked or slowed partway through the month
blockers.cause: The workspace hit its monthly call limit: 1,000 on Free (blocked after a one-time 30-day grace) or 100,000 on Team (slowed to 2 requests/sec).
blockers.fix: Cache aggressively, use webhooks, and tell Free-plan customers about the cap.

blockers.symptom: Users get sent back through consent after a quiet period
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens expire after 60 days unused.
blockers.fix: Refresh idle connections on a schedule well inside 60 days.

blockers.cause: The token was recently refreshed, so the request conflicted. Each refresh invalidates the previous pair.
blockers.fix: Serialize refreshes per connection and use the most recent tokens.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 60 minutes and refresh tokens 60 days. Refresh rotates both, and you can keep refreshing indefinitely as long as each refresh happens within the window.

Users pick the bases or workspaces a token can reach, and can grant 'All current and future bases in all current and future workspaces'. Grants can change at any time, so re-list bases instead of caching the list.
Monthly API quotas apply per workspace and are shared with every other integration in that workspace. Business and Enterprise have unlimited monthly calls.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Free and Team figures are from Airtable support. Business/Enterprise 'unlimited' and the shared pool come from third-party docs.

nuances.text: Enterprise admins can see and revoke users' OAuth grants from the Admin Panel's Third-party integrations tab.
Airtable's OAuth metadata advertises a dynamic client registration endpoint (/oauth2/v1/register), likely meant for MCP clients. Production apps should still register at airtable.com/create/oauth.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Seen in https://airtable.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server on 2026-10-20. The recommendation is our inference.
